activity.notes: Roman Dmowski was a principal leader of Polish National Democracy and one of the central diplomatic figures in the restoration of Polish independence, including leadership of the Polish National Committee and representation of Poland at the Paris Peace Conference. Because ATLAS requires a direct person–polity Activity, this registration uses his formally bounded service as Poland's Foreign Minister from 27 October to 14 December 1923; his broader independence and nationalist leadership is preserved in notes rather than converted into a fabricated state office.

sources.title: 86. rocznica śmierci Romana Dmowskiego — Instytut Pamięci Narodowej
sources.citation_text: Poland's Institute of National Remembrance identifies Dmowski as a leader of National Democracy, chairman of the Polish National Committee, Polish delegate and Versailles signatory, member of parliament, and Foreign Minister from 27 October to 14 December 1923.

sources.title: Roman Dmowski – jeden z ojców polskiej niepodległości — Instytut Pamięci Narodowej
sources.citation_text: The IPN biography describes Dmowski as a leader of the national camp, diplomat and co-creator of independent Poland, including his Paris diplomacy and later service as Foreign Minister.
